text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: realtime SLO alert — p95=1.35s (baseline 0.45s), p99=3.8s (baseline 1.2s). Streaming tail latency spikes observed across us-west1 edge nodes. Alert rule: realtime.p95p99 > threshold. Dash: https://dash.redwood/inference/realtime-latency
sanjay: paging oncall — looks like a sudden tail surge tied to edge-node e-uw1-*. Any immediate customer impact seen?
maria: checking KV cache hit rate now — running quick query
maria: ```curl -s "https://metrics.redwood/api/query?expr=kvcache_hit_ratio{region=\"us-west1\"}" | jq .```  hit ratio down ~18% last 3m, eviction spikes at ~02:14 UTC
emma: also seeing an increase in queue_depth and per-shard CPU on e-uw1. No error-rate increase (5xx steady). Likely workload pattern causing cold KV misses + batching delays.
sanjay: good call. Can we route traffic away from e-uw1 to eu-01 for short window? Need to avoid client-facing regressions.
leo: I'm oncall, taking this. Quick mitigations I can do now:
- enable routing fallback: prefer-region=eu-01 for realtime routes
- bump dedicated pool autoscale_min by +10 for us-west1 (if capacity available)
- temporarily lower max_batch_ms for streaming paths to reduce tail
leo: commands I'll run:
leo: ```
# flip routing to prefer eu
redwood routing set-preference --route realtime --pref-region eu-01 --reason "live tail mitigation"
# scale us-west pool
redwood pool update --name us-west-dedicated --min-instances 30
# decrease streaming batch window
redwood config set --key streaming.max_batch_ms --value 15
```
sanjay: +1 to all. Emma, can you watch the dashboard and confirm client p50/p95 after the flip?
emma: watching — pushing a short synthetic load to verify. Also opening a quick trace on a few slow sessions to inspect KV-get latencies.
maria: FYI kvcache eviction keys show a pattern for long prefix requests from a small client subset — might be a bad consumer pattern.
leo: routing flip initiated. APICall: OK 202. Pool scale requested. Batch config update OK.
emma: i see p95 dropping already from 1.35s -> 0.7s at 10s post-flip. p99 still high but trending down. queue_depth trending down too.
sanjay: any sign of customer-facing errors? Need to decide if we keep paging or mark as mitigated.
emma: error-rate still stable. A handful of long streams (clients X,Y) still heavy; tracing shows repeated long-prefix writes causing repeated cache churn.
maria: capturing list of top culprit client_ids, will DM sec-team to throttle as temporary measure.
leo: leaving the pref-region flip in place for 15m, then we'll progressively revert if stable. I'm staying on this until p99 < 1.5s for 5m.
incident-bot: note: page opened #INC-4321, priority=P1, assigned=leo
sanjay: thanks — good quick actions. After stable window, let's run a postmortem: include kvcache sizing, routing policy fuzz tests, and a synthetic workload that mimics the bad client pattern.
leo: agreed. I'll annotate the incident ticket with commands run, timestamps, and affected nodes.
emma: p99 at 0.9s now, p95=0.44s. queue and CPU normalized. I'll keep monitoring for 10 more minutes.
maria: saved logs and raw eviction traces to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-4321/ for the postmortem.
sanjay: ok, if no regressions in 10m we can close the live paging and continue investigation offline. Great run everyone :thumbsup:
leo: standing by until then. If anyone sees a new spike ping me directly.
emma: copy — monitoring continues.
maria: follow-up owners: kvcache infra (maria), routing (sanjay), client-throttling (sec-team).
leo: closing note here at 5990000245 — mitigation stable, handing to follow-up owners. Will update ticket.
